chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Muhammad narrated to us. He said: al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated to us from Jamil ibn Salih from 'Abdullah ibn Ghalib from Abu 'Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him).

He said: A believer ought to have eight characteristics: dignified in calamities, patient in tribulation, grateful in prosperity, content with what God has provided him, he does not wrong his enemies, nor does he burden his friends, his body toils but the people are at ease because of him.
Surely, knowledge is the intimate friend of the believer, forbearance is his vizier, patience is the commander of his forces, kindness is his brother, and gentleness is his father.

key_terms.الحلم: Forbearance — not mere patience but the composure to refrain from retaliating when wronged
key_terms.الرفق: Kindness/gentleness in dealing with others, associated with ease and mercy
key_terms.اللين: Softness/pliability — the quality of not being harsh or rigid in character
key_terms.الهزاهز: Calamities, disturbances, great tribulations — the word connotes violent upheavals
key_terms.وزير: Vizier — a trusted minister, the closest advisor to a ruler

ai.seo_question: What eight characteristics should a believer have according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) outlines eight moral traits that define a true believer: dignity under pressure, patience in trials, gratitude in good times, contentment with divine provision, justice toward enemies, consideration for friends, personal sacrifice for communal wellbeing, and a self-restraining character. The hadith then extends this ethical portrait through a vivid metaphor depicting knowledge, forbearance, patience, kindness, and gentleness as spiritual companions — a vizier, commander, brother, and father — that support the believer's inner life. This teaching was transmitted in the Imam's assembly to shape the conduct of his followers, emphasizing that virtue is not passive but an active, structured way of being in the world.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutwakkil (rh) narrated to us. He said: `Abdullah b. Ja`far al-Himyari narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Muhammad narrated to us. He said: Al-Hasan b. Mahbub narrated to us from Jamil b. Salih from `Abdullah b. Ghalib from Abi `Abdillah al-Sadiq (as).

He said: A believer should have eight characteristics: (1) [they should be] dignified with calamities, (2) patient with tribulation, (3) thankful when relaxed, and (4) content with what Allah has given him of sustenance. (5) He should not wrong the enemies, and (6) he should not be a burden on his friends. (7) He should tire his body, and (8) the people should be at ease because of him.
Surely, knowledge is the friend of the believer; forbearance is his vizier, patience is the commander of his forces, kindness is his brother, and gentleness is his father.
